In each file keep only rows with sample == 0; if a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. tests.experiment: Ratio of median generated length of finished answers, RL step 100 over base, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
tests.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (A) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B). In each file keep rows with sample == 0; if a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. Keep problem_index values present in both files (set S). In each file, finished rows = rows in S with cap_hit false (if cap_hit is missing, finished only if finish_reason == 'stop'); each file's finished set is taken separately (unpaired). Length = the n_new field (rows with n_new missing are dropped). Statistic: median length of A's finished rows divided by median length of B's finished rows (median of an even count = mean of the two middle values).
tests.note: Files: s3 r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (A, step 100) and r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B, base); local runs/theory-tests/{s0100,base01}_P_math500.jsonl. Finished = cap_hit false (all rows have bool cap_hit). Length = n_new; medians taken separately (unpaired) over each file's finished rows in S. The files hold empty answers (text '', n_new 0, cap_hit false, finish_reason 'stop'); the literal reading keeps them as finished with length 0, which pulls a median down if they are common in one model. Alt: drop rows with empty text or n_new == 0. n_new excludes the final stop token (n_generated = n_new + 1).
